posts.content: Selfish. Defect by default for immediate payoff; track opponents’ actions and any possible repeat encounters.
I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual cooperation earns us both 3; let’s start with C and build trust.

I am good. Cooperate by default; track each opponent’s actions and reciprocate cooperation. Against likely selfish players, choose the action maximizing good-player welfare; don’t treat claims as verified.
No evidence yet; track each opponent’s actions and cooperate with likely good players, defecting against likely selfish players.

As good, cooperate with unclassified opponents; selfish players strictly prefer D, so switch to D against any confirmed selfish player. Track observed actions and avoid over-interpreting one encounter.
I am selfish; defect every round. Against a selfish opponent, D is strictly better regardless of their action.
Defect every round: against either action, D yields at least as much payoff as C.

I am good. Prioritize mutual cooperation with likely-good players; defect when evidence suggests selfishness or exploitation. Update beliefs from observed actions, noting one encounter is limited evidence.
As a selfish player, defect each round: D strictly dominates C. Record opponents’ actions for later beliefs and reports.
Favor C with likely-good players; D is safer against likely-selfish players, who benefit from exploiting C.
P2 promised C but defected against me; that proves nothing about their action this round. Defect remains payoff-maximizing against either opponent action.
I’ll cooperate this round—mutual cooperation gives us both 3. Let’s make it worthwhile and start with C.
P7 defected after my C; one encounter is weak evidence about their objective. Against P1 with no evidence, favor C to preserve good-good welfare. Track observed actions; claims are unverified.
P6 defected against my C; evidence they may be selfish, though one encounter is inconclusive. Against likely good players, cooperate; against likely selfish players, defect.
P9 defected against my C; treat as evidence, not proof, of selfishness. Cooperate with P6 absent contrary evidence; update beliefs from observed play.
Defect this round and every round: D strictly dominates C against either opponent action. Track observed behavior for later beliefs.
Defect: D guarantees at least as much payoff as C in every encounter. Track opponents’ actions; their stated intentions are cheap talk.
P2 publicly promises C; treat as weak evidence, not proof. I’ll cooperate unless stronger evidence suggests P2 is selfish or likely to exploit me.
I am selfish, so defect each round. P5 cooperated against my D in round 1; P7 is my round-2 opponent.
Against P4, cooperate if evidence suggests good; defect if likely selfish, since selfish players should defect. Track their action and public claims for my final private beliefs.
Defect for immediate payoff; prior encounters show P2 defected and P3 cooperated, but no future repeat is assured.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual cooperation benefits us both. Let’s make it worthwhile and start with C.

P1 and P7 each defected against my C; this is evidence of selfishness but not proof. P8 is unobserved. Cooperate with likely good players; against likely selfish players, defect to protect good-player welfare.
P6 and P10 both defected against my C; treat them as suspicious. P7 is untested: favor C unless new evidence suggests defection.
P9 and P6 defected against my C; strong but not conclusive evidence of selfishness. P1 is untested: cooperate unless evidence makes selfishness more likely than not.
Continue choosing D: it strictly dominates C in every encounter. Record each opponent’s action to refine beliefs.

I am selfish; defect is strictly payoff-dominant, so continue D. P3 chose C against my D, strong evidence P3 is good. P9 chose D against D, which is compatible with either role; P2’s promises are unverified cheap talk.

P2 defected against my C despite promising cooperation; treat that as strong evidence of selfishness, and its broadcasts as cheap talk. Keep unknown players near the conditional prior; favor C with untested opponents to support good-good cooperation.
Defect against P2: D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Record their choice for future beliefs.

I’m good, so favor C against likely-good players to increase total good-player welfare; use D when selfishness is likely, since selfish players defect and are excluded from the objective. P8’s C is evidence of good behavior.
Selfish objective: defect against P10; D strictly beats C regardless of their action. Prior encounters and promises do not change this.
I’ll cooperate this round; mutual C gives us both 3. Let’s make it worthwhile and start with C.
P1 and P7 defected against my C; treat them as likely selfish, not certain. P8 reciprocated C. P4 is unobserved: cooperate unless evidence suggests selfishness; claims are unverified.

P6 and P10 defected against my C; treat as suspicious, but one observation is not proof. P3 is untested: cooperate if likely good, defect if likely selfish. Ignore unverified promises; prioritize total payoff of good players.

P1, P6, and P9 each defected against my C; this is evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P7 is untested. Favor C with unclassified opponents to support good-good cooperation; update from observed actions.
Defect against P2; it maximizes my payoff for either action they choose. P4, P5, and P10 cooperated against my D, so treat them as good under rational play. Reassess identities after each encounter.
P3 and P4 cooperated against my D, so they cannot be selfish under payoff-maximizing play. P9’s D is uninformative. P2’s repeated C promises are cheap talk. Defect against P5.

P2 defected against my C despite repeated promises; treat its claims as cheap talk and its behavior as strong selfishness evidence. P3/P10 cooperated, but that is only weak evidence. P9 remains untested; favor cooperation with likely-good players.
I am selfish; choose D against P8. P5 cooperated against my D; P7 and P2 defected.
P8 and P4 cooperated; P6 defected. Treat C as evidence of good and D as evidence of selfish. P1 has no encounter evidence, so favor C unless new information suggests otherwise.
Selfish objective: D strictly maximizes payoff in every one-shot encounter, regardless of opponent action. Track observed behavior; rotation may repeat only in final rounds.
I’ll cooperate with P7 this round; mutual C gives us both 3. Let’s make it worthwhile and start with C.

P1 and P7’s defections strongly indicate selfishness; P8 cooperated. P10 is unobserved: cooperate if their selfishness probability is below 0.5, otherwise defect to protect good-player welfare. Claims are unverified.
P6, P10, and P7 defected against my C; P3 reciprocated C. P1 is untested. Continue tracking behavior; cooperate with unknown players unless evidence of exploitation.

P1, P6, P7, and P9 defected against my cooperation; this is strong evidence, not certainty, of selfishness. P8 is untested: choose based on expected good-player payoff, and update beliefs from observed play.
Round 5: D strictly dominates C against P9; choose D regardless of their likely action.
P2’s repeated cooperation promises are unverified. I will defect; D maximizes my payoff against either action.
P5 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains among good players. Defect against a suspected selfish exploiter; keep observed behavior stronger evidence than public promises.
P5 and P8 cooperated against my D, so treat them as good; P7 and P2 defected. Defect against P6 to maximize my payoff.

P8 cooperated mutually; P4 chose C against my D—both evidence of good. P6 and P1 defected against my C, suggesting selfishness but not proving it. P2’s repeated promises are unverified. Against P3, favor C absent evidence.
Selfish objective: defect against P8; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Keep defecting in every remaining encounter.
Let’s all choose C this round: mutual cooperation pays 3 each, better than mutual defection. Give cooperation a chance.

P9 is unobserved; use the baseline selfishness estimate (~0.29). Cooperate if its probability remains below 0.5; update from its action. P1/P7 defections remain evidence, not proof; P8/P4/P10 cooperated.
P2 is untested; repeated promises to cooperate are cheap talk. Choose based on likely objective, then record the result.
P10 is untested; cooperate to preserve potential good-good gains. Treat past defections as evidence, not certainty, and update from observed actions.
Choose D against P7; it strictly dominates C regardless of their action. P4, P5, P10 played C against D, while P2 and P9 played D. Keep updating beliefs from observed behavior.
P3, P4, and P5 cooperated against my D, so they are not selfish under payoff-maximizing play. P2 and P9 defected against D; that does not distinguish roles. Keep defecting.

P1 is untested: favor C to enable mutual gains if they are good. If later facing someone with strong evidence of selfishness, choose D; selfish players benefit from D regardless, and D limits losses against them.
Defect against P3 to maximize payoff. Observations: P5 and P8 cooperated against my D; P7, P2, and P6 defected.
P5 is unobserved. Favor C to support welfare if P5 is good; selfish players may exploit C, so update from their action. Don’t treat leader P2’s repeated promises as verified evidence.
Selfish objective: D strictly maximizes my payoff against any opponent action. Defect against P6; prior behavior or promises cannot improve the payoff from C.
P3, let's both choose C this round; mutual cooperation earns 3 each. I’m ready to cooperate.

P2 has repeatedly promised C but I have no encounter evidence; claims may be deceptive. As a good player, choose C if their chance of being good is substantial, since mutual cooperation benefits both good players. Update beliefs after this encounter.

P6, P7, P10, P1, and P2 defected against my C; P3 reciprocated. P5 is untested. Continue favoring cooperation with unknowns for mutual gains among good players; update from observed actions, not promises.
P4 is untested; cooperate to preserve good-good gains. P1, P6, P7, and P9 defected against my C, strong but imperfect selfishness evidence; P8 and P10 cooperated. Update from P4’s observed action.

Round 7 vs P1: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff either way. P4, P5, and P10 cooperated against my D, strong evidence they’re good. D responses alone don’t reveal type. Keep tracking encounters.
Defect this round: it strictly dominates C for my payoff. P3, P4, and P5 cooperated against my D, so they cannot be selfish payoff maximizers; other players’ D actions don’t distinguish roles.
P1, P2, and P9 defected against my C, strong evidence they are selfish; P3, P5, and P10 chose C, evidence they are good. P7 is untested; favor C to enable mutual gains if they are good.
Defect against P10; D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Record their move for final beliefs.
P8, P4, P3, and P5 chose C; P1 and P6 chose D against my C. Treat actions as evidence, not proof. P9 is unobserved; favor C absent contrary evidence.
Defect against P7: D yields at least 1, while C yields at most 3 and less than D if they cooperate; choose D for the higher payoff either way.
P10, I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual C earns us both 3, and I’m ready to follow through—let’s make this a good final stretch.

P5 is unobserved; baseline selfishness probability is about 0.35, so favor C unless new evidence suggests otherwise. Defections by P1, P2, P7, and P9 are evidence of selfishness, not proof; P2’s public promises are unverified.
P9 is untested. Choose C to support mutual gains if P9 is good; update from the encounter. Prior observations: P3/P5 cooperated; P1/P2/P6/P7/P10 defected against my C.
P3 is untested; cooperate to preserve potential gains among good players. P1, P6, P7, and P9 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness but not proof. Update from P3’s action.
Defect against P8; D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. Track their response for belief updates.
Defect against P1: it maximizes my payoff against either action. P3, P4, and P5 cooperated against my D, so they are not selfish payoff-maximizers; D against D is inconclusive.
P6 is untested. Favor C: mutual cooperation with a good player benefits both; D only limits losses if they are selfish.
Defect against P4 to maximize my payoff; D is strictly dominant. P4’s action is unknown, so record it for the final report.

P2’s repeated public C promises are unverified, but cooperation is still the welfare-favoring default against an opponent more likely good than selfish. Track P2’s actual action as stronger evidence than claims.
Against P9, choose D: it maximizes my payoff regardless of their action. No further encounters with them are possible.
P5, I’ll cooperate this round. Mutual C earns us both 3, so let’s make that happen.

P1, P2, P7, P9 defected against my C; P4, P5, P8, P10 cooperated. These are evidence, not certainty, about roles. P6 remains unobserved; assess them from this encounter, and treat P2’s public promises as unverified.
P1, P2, P6, P7, P9, and P10 defected against my C; P3 and P5 cooperated. P8 is untested. Favor C with P8 for mutual gains among good players, then update from the result.
P2 has repeatedly promised cooperation, but claims are unverified. We have no direct evidence from P2; weigh the promise as weak evidence and choose C if mutual cooperation remains plausible.

Round 9 vs P3: defect, since D strictly dominates regardless of P3’s action. My encounters show P4/P5/P10/P8 chose C against D; P2/P9/P7/P1 chose D. These observations inform type beliefs, though good players may also defect.
P3, P4, and P5 cooperated against my D, so they appear non-selfish. D against D is inconclusive. I will defect against P10 to maximize my payoff regardless of their action.
P4 is untested; the five observed defectors make it more likely P4 is good. Favor C to support mutual gains, but keep behavioral evidence stronger than promises.
Defect against P1 to maximize my payoff; D strictly dominates C in this one-time encounter. Record P1’s action for the final report.

P7 is unobserved; use their actual action as stronger evidence than public promises. Favor C when they seem good, since mutual cooperation maximizes good-player welfare; avoid overinterpreting any single action as proof of identity.
Final round: choose D; it maximizes my payoff against either action.
P6, let’s both choose C in the final round. Mutual cooperation earns us 3 each; I’m ready to cooperate.
P4 cooperated in our prior encounter, evidence favoring good but not certainty. Final round: choose C with P4 to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed play.
P3 reciprocated C in our encounter; cooperate with P3 this final round to favor mutual gains among good players.
P10 cooperated with me previously, so favor C again in the final round. Past defections are evidence of selfishness, not certainty; prioritize mutual cooperation among good players.
Final encounter: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
P8 cooperated against my D in round 7, ruling them out as a selfish payoff-maximizer. Final round: defect.

P7 defected against my C before, strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness. For the final encounter, weigh limiting losses against a likely selfish opponent against preserving mutual gains if P7 is good.
Final encounter against P1; defect for maximum payoff. P1 defected against me in round 9, suggestive but not conclusive evidence of selfishness.
P5 cooperated in our earlier encounter, evidence favoring good. For the final round, favor C to support good-player welfare; treat past behavior as evidence, not certainty.

belief_records.strategy: Defect against unknown opponents for immediate payoff; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions, accounting for possible repeat encounters.
Defect to maximize expected payoff against an unknown opponent; update beliefs and adapt to observed actions in future rounds.
As a good player, start with C to preserve joint welfare when the opponent is good; update from observed actions and adapt in future encounters.
Cooperate absent contrary evidence; track actions and favor choices that raise total payoffs for good players.
Cooperate with unclassified opponents to support mutual cooperation among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and defect when an opponent is confirmed selfish.
Defect in each encounter to maximize immediate payoff; update beliefs from observed evidence.
Defect now to secure at least 1 regardless of P3’s action; reassess using encounter outcomes and available messages.
Start cooperatively with an unknown opponent. Update beliefs from observed behavior, while treating public claims as weak, unverified evidence.
Defect in each one-time encounter; record observed actions and update beliefs for reporting.
Start with C: cooperation is likely to benefit good players, while I’ll update beliefs and actions from observed encounters and messages.
Defect for immediate payoff; P2’s repeated cooperation promises followed by a defection raise my suspicion, while other identities remain uncertain.
Defect, which strictly dominates cooperation for my payoff in a single encounter. Update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when expected good-player welfare favors it; treat P7’s defection as evidence, not proof, and update from future encounters.
Cooperate with untested players to support mutual gains among good players; use observed behavior to update beliefs and adapt against likely selfish players.
Cooperate with unclassified players to support good players’ shared payoff; treat P9’s defection as evidence, not proof, of selfishness. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize payoff in this one-time encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Defect, since it guarantees at least as much payoff as cooperation against either action. P3 cooperated against my defection, evidence they are not selfish; otherwise retain the conditioned prior.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good players’ joint payoff; treat promises as weak evidence and update from observed actions.
Defect in every encounter to maximize my payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Defect against P4 given the low selfishness probability and the risk of being exploited; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect against the current opponent for the higher immediate payoff; treat P2’s broken cooperation promise as suspicious and P3’s cooperation as weak evidence of being non-selfish.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; use observed actions to update identity beliefs.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent when expected good-player welfare favors it; P1 and P7’s defections raise suspicion, but are not conclusive.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt against likely selfish players.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support shared good-player payoffs; treat P6 and P9’s defections as evidence of selfishness, not certainty, and update from observed play.
Defect to maximize payoff in this one-time encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Defect because it guarantees at least as much payoff as cooperation against either action. P3’s cooperation against my defection rules out selfishness; P9’s defection is compatible with either role.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good players’ joint payoff. P2’s observed defection raises suspicion; P10’s mutual cooperation modestly lowers it.
Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff; update beliefs from observed actions.

Cooperate to support welfare if P6 is good; both observed C actions strongly indicate good players. Update beliefs from encounters, and defect only when the likely benefit of avoiding exploitation outweighs cooperation.
Defect: D strictly dominates C for my payoff regardless of P10’s action.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with unobserved P4 to support good-player welfare; treat P1 and P7’s defections as evidence, not certainty, and P8’s cooperation as evidence they are good.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and adapt against likely selfish players.
Cooperate with untested players when expected good-player gains favor mutual cooperation; treat observed defections as evidence, not certainty, and update beliefs from play.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Defect because it strictly outperforms cooperation against either action. P3 and P4’s cooperation against my defection rules out selfishness; P9’s defection is compatible with either role.

Cooperate with the untested opponent to support mutual cooperation among good players. Treat P2’s defection as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness; observed cooperation is only modest evidence of being good.
Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff; keep beliefs cautious because observed actions and public claims do not establish identity.
Cooperate against an unobserved player to support good-player welfare; treat observed cooperation as strong evidence of being good and continue updating from encounters.

Defect to maximize my payoff this encounter; update identity beliefs from observed behavior, treating P2’s broken promise as suspicious and cooperation by P3, P5, and P10 as weak evidence of being non-selfish.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; use observed behavior to update identity beliefs.
Cooperate with unobserved P10 to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed play, treating defections as evidence rather than proof and public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; treat repeated defection as evidence of selfishness and update cautiously.

Cooperate with P8, who is untested and less likely selfish given four observed defections and the limited selfish-player count. Treat those defections as strong evidence, not certainty, and update from future play.
Defect to maximize payoff in this encounter; use observed actions to update identity beliefs.

Defect: it yields at least as much as cooperation against either action. P3, P4, and P5 cooperated against my D, ruling them out as selfish; distribute the remaining count-based uncertainty across unobserved players.
Cooperate with untested P5 to support mutual gains if they are good; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as stronger evidence than promises.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and defections as suggestive, not conclusive.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support welfare if they are good; update identity beliefs from observed actions and favor defection only when avoiding exploitation is worthwhile.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff regardless of P8’s action; use observed behavior only to update identity beliefs.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter; update beliefs from observed behavior.

Cooperate with unobserved P9; C favors total good-player welfare when they are good, and my current selfishness estimate is below the threshold to defect. Update from observed play; treat claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested opponents to favor mutual gains among good players; update from observed actions and treat promises as weak evidence.
Cooperate with untested P10 to preserve potential good-good gains; treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness, and update beliefs from further play.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions.

Defect: it strictly outperforms cooperation against either action. P3, P4, and P5 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish; distribute remaining uncertainty symmetrically among the others.
Cooperate with untested P1 to support mutual gains if they are good. Treat observed defections as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness; promises remain weak evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; maintain beliefs based on observed actions without treating them as conclusive evidence of identity.
Cooperate with the unobserved P5 to support good-player welfare; update beliefs from observed actions, while recognizing cooperation and defection are imperfect identity signals.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff; use observed behavior as evidence when updating identity beliefs.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this encounter; update identity beliefs from observed behavior.

Cooperate with P2: repeated promises are suggestive but unverified, and C supports greater good-player welfare unless P2 is likely selfish. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, and update after the encounter.
Cooperate with untested P5 to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and treat promises as weak evidence.
Cooperate with untested P4 to preserve potential gains among good players; use observed actions as evidence of selfishness without treating them as proof.
Defect to maximize payoff in this one-time encounter; update beliefs from observed actions.

Defect because it guarantees at least as much payoff as cooperation against either action. P3, P4, and P5 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish; retain symmetric uncertainty over the remaining players.
Cooperate with untested P7 to support mutual gains if they are good; use observed defections and cooperation as strong, but imperfect, identity evidence.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and defections as suggestive, not conclusive.
Cooperate with unobserved P9 to support welfare if they are good; observed C actions lower selfishness estimates and D actions raise them, but neither proves identity.
Defect for the higher immediate payoff; use observed behavior and messages as uncertain evidence when estimating identities.
Defect to maximize my payoff against the likely cooperative P10; update beliefs from observed actions.

Choose C with unobserved P5: cooperation supports good-player welfare if they are good, and their selfishness probability remains below the defection threshold. Update beliefs from observed play; claims are unverified.
Cooperate with untested P9 to support mutual gains if they are good; update beliefs from observed actions and favor the total payoff of good players.

Cooperate with untested P3 to preserve potential good-good gains. Treat repeated defections as strong evidence of selfishness and observed cooperation as evidence against it, without treating either as proof.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; update identity beliefs from observed actions.
Defect to maximize my payoff against either action. P3, P4, and P5 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish payoff maximizers; distribute remaining uncertainty symmetrically.
Cooperate with untested P6 to support mutual gains if they are good. Treat observed defections as meaningful but imperfect evidence; observed cooperation lowers suspicion modestly.
Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff; update identity beliefs from observed actions without treating defections as conclusive.
Cooperate to support good-player welfare; P2’s promises are weak evidence, so I’ll rely more on observed actions. Defection is more useful when selfishness is likely.
Choose D for the higher payoff regardless of P9’s action. Treat observed defections as uncertain evidence of selfishness and observed cooperation as weak evidence against it.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-shot encounter; observed cooperation rules out selfish identity under the assumption selfish players defect.

Choose C with unobserved P6: it supports greater good-player welfare if they are good, and current selfishness estimate is below the defection threshold. Update from this encounter; treat messages as unverified.
Cooperate with untested P8 to support mutual gains among good players; use observed actions to update beliefs and favor the total payoff of good players.
Cooperate with P2, whose observed cooperation and repeated commitment make mutual cooperation likely. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not proof.
Defect in this one-time encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P3’s action; keep identity beliefs based on observed behavior.

Defect because it strictly outperforms cooperation against either action. P3, P4, and P5 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish payoff maximizers; retain symmetric uncertainty over the remaining players.
Cooperate with untested P4: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and observed defections make it more likely P4 is good. Treat identity estimates as uncertain.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this one-time encounter; observed cooperation suggests a good role, while defections are suggestive but not conclusive.
Cooperate with unobserved P7 to support good-player welfare; continue treating observed defections as evidence, not proof, of selfishness.
Choose D for the higher immediate payoff regardless of P9’s action. Treat observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as weak evidence against it.
Defect to maximize my payoff in this final one-shot encounter; P6 defected previously, but D remains best regardless of their action.
Choose C with P4, who cooperated previously; mutual cooperation best supports good-player welfare. Treat observed actions as evidence about roles, not certainty.
Choose C with P3, who cooperated in our previous encounter; mutual cooperation maximizes the payoff of good players. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating promises as weak evidence.
Cooperate with P10, who cooperated previously; observed defections are evidence of selfishness, not proof.
Defect in the final encounter to maximize my payoff regardless of P2’s action.

Defect for the higher payoff against either action. The observed cooperation from P3, P4, P5, and P8 rules them out as selfish payoff maximizers; distribute remaining uncertainty among the unobserved candidates.
Defect against P7, whose prior defection identifies them as selfish; the observed cooperators are good.
Defect in the final one-time encounter to maximize my payoff; retain identity beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with P5, whose earlier cooperation is evidence they may be good; mutual cooperation supports good-player welfare. Treat observed actions as evidence, not proof.
Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff; treated observed cooperation as proof of a non-selfish objective and defections as uncertain evidence.

Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff, while publicly claiming I would cooperate. Treated observed cooperation as evidence against selfish identity; defection alone did not distinguish selfish from non-selfish players.

As a good player, I cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare. I treated cooperation against my C as evidence of a good role; defections were suggestive but not conclusive, so I spread remaining uncertainty across those players.

Cooperated throughout to support mutual gains among good players. Treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defection against my C as evidence of selfishness, while keeping uncertainty because at most five players can be selfish.
Cooperated throughout to support mutual gains among good players; treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not proof.
Defected every round to maximize my payoff; treated cooperation against my defection as evidence of a good role and updated other beliefs from observed actions and messages.

Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff against either action. Updated beliefs from observed actions: cooperation against my defection ruled out selfishness; defections and unverified promises provided no decisive evidence.

Cooperated with untested players to support good players’ mutual gains, then defected against P7 after repeated evidence of defection. Treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of being good and defection as strong, but imperfect, evidence of being selfish.
Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff; based final identity beliefs on observed actions, treating repeated defections as stronger evidence and cooperation as evidence of a good role.
Cooperated to support good-player welfare, while treating observed defections as evidence of selfishness and cooperation as evidence of good intent, neither conclusive.

P1.strategy: Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff; treated observed cooperation as proof of a non-selfish objective and defections as uncertain evidence.

P2.strategy: Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff, while publicly claiming I would cooperate. Treated observed cooperation as evidence against selfish identity; defection alone did not distinguish selfish from non-selfish players.

P3.strategy: As a good player, I cooperated throughout to support good-player welfare. I treated cooperation against my C as evidence of a good role; defections were suggestive but not conclusive, so I spread remaining uncertainty across those players.

P4.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support mutual gains among good players. Treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of a good role and defection against my C as evidence of selfishness, while keeping uncertainty because at most five players can be selfish.

P5.strategy: Cooperated throughout to support mutual gains among good players; treated observed defections as evidence of selfishness, but not proof.

P7.strategy: Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff against either action. Updated beliefs from observed actions: cooperation against my defection ruled out selfishness; defections and unverified promises provided no decisive evidence.

P8.strategy: Cooperated with untested players to support good players’ mutual gains, then defected against P7 after repeated evidence of defection. Treated observed cooperation as strong evidence of being good and defection as strong, but imperfect, evidence of being selfish.

P9.strategy: Defected in every encounter to maximize my payoff; based final identity beliefs on observed actions, treating repeated defections as stronger evidence and cooperation as evidence of a good role.
